name: Azure Virtual Network
whatItIs: An isolated network with address spaces and subnets where Azure resources communicate privately, connect to other VNets and to on-premises.
primaryPurpose: Private networking foundation for IaaS and many PaaS services.
networking: Regional resource; 5 reserved IPs per subnet; non-overlapping spaces required for peering/hybrid
pricing: VNets are free; pay for peering data transfer, public IPs, gateways and other attached services.

confusedWith.name: Subnet
confusedWith.difference: A subnet is a range inside a VNet; NSGs and route tables attach to subnets.

relevanceNote: VNets, subnets, peering, public IPs and routes are core networking skills.

name: Network Security Groups
tagline: Stateful L3/L4 traffic filtering for subnets and NICs.
whatItIs: A set of prioritized allow/deny rules evaluated against a packet's 5-tuple, associated with subnets and/or network interfaces.
primaryPurpose: Control which traffic may reach or leave Azure resources.
useCases: Allowing only load balancer and app traffic
security: Applies to everyone/everything in the subnet/NIC
networking: Regional; associate with subnets and NICs in the same region
pricing: No charge (flow logs and Traffic Analytics are billed separately).

confusedWith.name: Azure Firewall
confusedWith.difference: Central L3–L7 firewall with FQDN filtering; NSGs are distributed L3/L4 filters.

relevanceNote: Creating NSGs/ASGs and evaluating effective rules are explicit skills.
examTips: Inbound: subnet NSG then NIC NSG

name: Azure Firewall
whatItIs: A cloud-native firewall service with built-in high availability, autoscaling, threat intelligence and L3–L7 filtering.
primaryPurpose: Centrally inspect and control traffic between networks and to the internet.
keyFeatures: Premium: TLS inspection, IDPS, URL filtering
security: Combine with UDRs to force traffic through it
Use Firewall Policy for central management
networking: Requires AzureFirewallSubnet (/26); typically in a hub VNet
pricing: Hourly deployment charge by SKU (Basic, Standard, Premium) plus per-GB processed.

confusedWith.name: NSG
confusedWith.difference: Free, distributed L3/L4 filtering without FQDN rules.

confusedWith.name: Application Gateway WAF
confusedWith.difference: WAF protects inbound web apps at L7; Firewall controls general network traffic.

relevanceNote: Not a named AZ-104 skill but frequently used in routing and security scenarios.
examTips: UDR 0.0.0.0/0 → firewall private IP to force tunnel through it

name: Azure Load Balancer
whatItIs: A regional TCP/UDP load balancer with public or internal frontends, health probes and rules.
primaryPurpose: Distribute network flows across healthy backend instances.
security: Standard SKU is closed by default; use NSGs
No inspection — pair with WAF/Firewall where needed
networking: Backends must be in one VNet; probes from 168.63.129.16
pricing: Standard: per rule-hour and per GB processed.

confusedWith.name: Application Gateway
confusedWith.difference: L7 HTTP routing with WAF and TLS termination.

relevanceNote: Configuring and troubleshooting internal/public load balancers is an explicit skill.
examTips: Health probe and NSG are the first things to check

name: Azure Application Gateway
tagline: Regional Layer 7 load balancer with WAF.
whatItIs: A web traffic load balancer that routes on host name and URL path, terminates TLS and can include a Web Application Firewall.
primaryPurpose: Secure and route HTTP(S) traffic to web backends in a region.
security: Key Vault certificates via managed identity
networking: Dedicated subnet; public and/or private frontend
pricing: Fixed hourly charge plus capacity units (v2).

confusedWith.name: Front Door
confusedWith.difference: Global edge L7 service; Application Gateway is regional.

relevanceNote: Common in load-balancing scenarios and comparisons.

name: Azure Front Door
tagline: Global edge entry point with CDN, L7 load balancing and WAF.
whatItIs: A global service on Microsoft's edge network that accelerates and load-balances HTTP(S) traffic across regions, with caching and WAF.
primaryPurpose: Global web application delivery and failover.
security: Lock origins to accept only Front Door traffic
networking: Global; origins can be public or (Premium) private via Private Link
pricing: Base fee by tier plus requests and data transfer.

confusedWith.name: Traffic Manager
confusedWith.difference: DNS-based global routing for any protocol; Front Door proxies HTTP(S) traffic.

relevanceNote: Mostly appears as a distractor in load-balancing questions.
examTips: Global + HTTP + WAF → Front Door; regional + HTTP → Application Gateway

name: Azure Traffic Manager
whatItIs: A DNS-based service that directs clients to endpoints in different regions using routing methods such as priority, weighted, performance and geographic.
primaryPurpose: Global failover and distribution for any internet-facing endpoint.
useCases: Routing users to the closest region
keyFeatures: Routing methods: priority, weighted, performance, geographic, multivalue, subnet
security: Doesn't inspect traffic — clients connect directly to endpoints
networking: Works at DNS level; any protocol
pricing: Per DNS query and per health-checked endpoint.

confusedWith.name: Load Balancer
confusedWith.difference: Regional L4 data-path balancing vs global DNS steering.

relevanceNote: Distractor in load-balancing and DNS questions.
examTips: DNS-based → clients cache answers; failover depends on TTL

name: Azure DNS
tagline: Host public and private DNS zones in Azure.
whatItIs: DNS hosting on Microsoft's global name servers for public domains, plus private DNS zones for name resolution within VNets.
primaryPurpose: Manage DNS records alongside your Azure resources.
keyFeatures: Private zones with VNet links and auto-registration
networking: Azure-provided DNS at 168.63.129.16; private zones are global resources linked to VNets
pricing: Per hosted zone per month and per million queries; Private Resolver endpoints billed hourly.

confusedWith.name: Domain registrar
confusedWith.difference: Azure DNS hosts zones; you still register domains elsewhere (or via App Service Domains).

relevanceNote: Configuring Azure DNS is an explicit skill.
examTips: Delegate by updating NS records at the registrar

name: Azure VPN Gateway
tagline: Encrypted hybrid connectivity over the internet.
whatItIs: A virtual network gateway that terminates site-to-site, point-to-site and VNet-to-VNet IPsec/IKE and SSL VPN connections.
primaryPurpose: Securely connect on-premises networks and clients to Azure VNets.
security: Certificate or Entra ID authentication for P2S
networking: Deployed in GatewaySubnet (/27+ recommended); needs a public IP
pricing: Hourly by gateway SKU plus outbound data transfer; some P2S connection counts are SKU-limited.
relevanceNote: Hybrid connectivity concepts appear frequently in networking scenarios.
examTips: Local network gateway = on-prem public IP + prefixes

name: Azure ExpressRoute
whatItIs: Dedicated private connectivity between your network and Microsoft cloud services through a connectivity provider.
primaryPurpose: Reliable, high-bandwidth, low-latency hybrid connectivity without the public internet.
security: Private but not encrypted by default — add MACsec (Direct) or IPsec over ER
networking: ExpressRoute gateway in GatewaySubnet; BGP routing
pricing: Circuit charge by bandwidth and plan (metered or unlimited data), plus gateway hours and provider fees.

confusedWith.name: Site-to-site VPN
confusedWith.difference: Encrypted over the internet with variable performance.

relevanceNote: Conceptual understanding is expected; detailed configuration is beyond AZ-104.

name: Azure Bastion
whatItIs: A managed jump-host service that provides secure RDP/SSH over TLS to VMs in a VNet and peered VNets.
primaryPurpose: Secure VM administration without exposing management ports.
networking: AzureBastionSubnet /26 or larger; Standard public IP (except Developer SKU)
pricing: Hourly by SKU and scale units plus outbound data; Developer SKU is free.

confusedWith.name: Point-to-site VPN
confusedWith.difference: Gives network-level access; Bastion gives per-VM sessions.

relevanceNote: Implementing Azure Bastion is an explicit skill.

name: Azure NAT Gateway
tagline: Scalable outbound internet connectivity for subnets.
whatItIs: A fully managed network address translation service that gives subnets outbound-only internet access through static public IPs.
primaryPurpose: Predictable, scalable egress without SNAT port exhaustion.
useCases: Allowlisting by a fixed egress IP
networking: Takes precedence over other outbound methods for its subnets
pricing: Hourly resource charge plus per-GB processed (and public IPs).

confusedWith.name: Load balancer outbound rules
confusedWith.difference: Also SNAT, but NAT Gateway is simpler, scales better and takes precedence.

relevanceNote: Appears in routing and outbound connectivity scenarios.

name: Azure Private Link (Private Endpoints)
tagline: Access PaaS services over a private IP in your VNet.
whatItIs: Private Link powers private endpoints — network interfaces with private IPs that connect privately to a specific Azure service resource or your own Private Link service.
primaryPurpose: Keep traffic to PaaS services private and disable public exposure.
useCases: Private access to Storage, SQL, Key Vault, App Service
On-premises access to PaaS via ExpressRoute/VPN
keyFeatures: Private Link service for your own apps
security: Disable public network access on the target
networking: Needs DNS so service FQDNs resolve to the private IP
pricing: Per endpoint-hour and per GB inbound/outbound processed.

confusedWith.name: Service endpoints
confusedWith.difference: Free subnet-level access to the service's public endpoint; no private IP.

relevanceNote: Configuring private endpoints for PaaS is explicitly listed.
examTips: Check DNS first when a private endpoint 'doesn't work'

name: Azure Network Watcher
whatItIs: Regional tools for connectivity diagnostics, packet capture, flow logging and connection monitoring.
primaryPurpose: Find out why traffic does or doesn't flow.
keyFeatures: VNet flow logs and Traffic Analytics
networking: Enabled per region automatically with VNets
pricing: Some tools free; charges for diagnostic checks beyond free amounts, Connection Monitor tests, flow logs and Traffic Analytics processing.

confusedWith.name: Azure Monitor metrics
confusedWith.difference: Aggregate metrics vs path- and flow-level diagnostics.

relevanceNote: Using Network Watcher and Connection Monitor is an explicit skill.
examTips: Blocked → IP flow verify; misrouted → next hop
